title: Tests: parse_did_key + verify_did_sig with external vectors
description:
What: Write tests for parse_did_key and verify_did_sig using externally-generated test vectors.

Test vector generation (external oracle — run ONCE with Python, hardcode results):
Use Python cryptography library to generate:
  from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
  import base64, struct
  # Ed25519 multicodec prefix
  MULTICODEC_ED25519 = b'\xed\x01'
  key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()  # use fixed test seed for reproducibility
  pub_bytes = key.public_key().public_bytes_raw()
  multibase_payload = MULTICODEC_ED25519 + pub_bytes
  import base58
  did_key_str = 'did:key:z' + base58.b58encode(multibase_payload).decode()
  article = b'From: alice@example.com\r\nSubject: DID test\r\n\r\nBody.\r\n'
  sig = key.sign(article)
  sig_b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sig).rstrip(b'=').decode()

Tests:
1. parse_did_key_valid: given hardcoded did:key, returns Ok(verifying_key) that matches expected public key bytes
2. parse_did_key_unsupported_method: did:web:example.com -> Err(UnsupportedMethod)
3. parse_did_key_bad_multicodec: base58btc-encoded 32 bytes with wrong multicodec prefix -> Err(InvalidKeyEncoding) or Err(UnsupportedMethod)
4. parse_did_key_wrong_key_length: truncated key -> Err(InvalidKeyEncoding)
5. verify_did_sig_valid: hardcoded article + correct sig -> Ok(true)
6. verify_did_sig_wrong_sig: same article, sig bytes XOR'd -> Ok(false)
7. verify_did_sig_wrong_article: correct sig but different article bytes -> Ok(false)
8. verify_did_sig_format_error: header_value with no space -> Err(InvalidFormat)
9. verify_did_sig_with_did_sig_header_present: article includes the X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header itself, verify_did_sig strips it and still returns Ok(true)

All hardcoded test vectors must come from the Python oracle above. Include the Python code as a comment in the test file showing how vectors were generated (but do not run Python at test time — tests must be offline).
